title: Ozone depletion & acid rain
examples: What are the main gases that cause acid rain?
How do CFCs affect the ozone layer?
Can we prevent acid rain from forming?

explain.say: Today we are learning about two environmental issues. We will look at ozone depletion and acid rain.
First we look at CFC radicals. Chlorofluorocarbons or CFCs were used in things like spray cans. These chemicals release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere.
These chlorine radicals then react with ozone gas. This reaction breaks down the ozone layer over time. This process is harmful to life.
Next we study the gases causing acid rain. Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides are the main culprits. These gases come from burning fossil fuels.

draw.text: SO₂ and NOx from burning fuels

explain.say: These gases react in the atmosphere. They mix with water vapor to form weak acids. This mixture is what causes acid rain.
In everyday life, car exhaust is a big source. Cars burn fuel releasing these harmful gases. This contributes to both acid rain and air pollution.

faq.q: What is the ozone layer, and why is it important?
faq.a: The ozone layer is a region in the Earth's stratosphere. It absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation. Asks: What protects Earth from UV rays? How do we keep ozone safe?
asks: Why do we need the ozone layer?

faq.q: What are CFCs, and why were they used in the past?
faq.a: CFCs are chlorofluorocarbons. They were used in things like refrigerants and aerosol sprays. They are now restricted because they harm the ozone layer.

faq.q: What is the main cause of acid rain?
faq.a: The main cause is the emission of sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. These gases come primarily from burning fossil fuels like coal.
asks: Where does acid rain come from?

faq.q: Does acid rain only come from factories?
faq.a: No, it can also come from vehicles and other sources. Any process burning fossil fuels can release these polluting gases. We must reduce all burning.
asks: Is it only industry causing acid rain?

faq.q: How can we stop ozone depletion?
faq.a: We can reduce the use of CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances. Governments have set international agreements to control these chemicals.
asks: What can we do about ozone depletion?
How do we protect the ozone layer?

facts: CFCs release chlorine atoms that destroy ozone.
Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides are key pollutants.
Burning fossil fuels releases these harmful gases.
Acid rain lowers the pH of natural water bodies.

quiz.say: Which gas is primarily responsible for depleting the ozone layer?
quiz.why: CFCs contain chlorine that reacts with ozone.

wrong.0: This gas is more linked to acid rain, not ozone depletion.
wrong.1: These are also linked to acid rain, not the ozone layer.
wrong.2: Water vapor is essential for life and does not deplete ozone.

quiz.say: Acid rain is primarily caused by which pair of gases?
quiz.why: These gases react with water to form weak acids in the atmosphere.

wrong.0: These gases are naturally present and do not cause acid rain.
wrong.1: These gases are mainly linked to the greenhouse effect.
wrong.2: These are more associated with ozone depletion.

quiz.say: If a factory burns coal, what two pollutants are most likely released?
quiz.why: Coal contains sulfur, releasing SO₂, and high heat releases NOx.

wrong.0: Oxygen is necessary for life, and ozone is what is being damaged.
wrong.1: These are products of incomplete burning, not the primary acid rain precursors.
wrong.2: While CO₂ is a pollutant, SO₂ and NOx are the direct acid rain precursors.
